blogs.title: How DeepSeekMath Brought Open-Source AI Closer to GPT-4 on Math
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the paper’s biggest achievement: how a 7B open model reached unusually strong performance on hard math benchmarks. This post would explain why mathematical reasoning is difficult for language models, what makes DeepSeekMath notable, and why its results matter for the open-source AI ecosystem.

blogs.title: The Secret Ingredient Was the Internet: Mining 120B Math Tokens from the Web
blogs.description: A deep dive into the paper’s data story, showing how the researchers built a massive math-focused training corpus from Common Crawl. The post would simplify the iterative filtering pipeline, explain why data quality mattered more than raw model size, and highlight how careful curation helped a smaller model outperform much larger ones.

blogs.title: Why Teaching AI to Code Can Make It Better at Math
blogs.description: This post would focus on one of the paper’s most interesting findings: starting from a code-trained model gave DeepSeekMath a major advantage. It would explain, in plain language, why programming and mathematical reasoning reinforce each other, and what this means for future AI training strategies.

blogs.title: GRPO Explained: The New Reinforcement Learning Trick Behind DeepSeekMath
blogs.description: A reader-friendly explanation of Group Relative Policy Optimization, the paper’s alternative to PPO. The blog would cover how GRPO works without a separate critic model, why that reduces memory costs, and how reinforcement learning improved the model’s math performance even after strong supervised fine-tuning.

blogs.title: Bigger Isn’t Always Better: What DeepSeekMath Teaches Us About Training Smarter AI
blogs.description: A lessons-learned post built around the paper’s broader insights: high-quality domain data can beat brute-force scale, arXiv papers were surprisingly less useful than expected, and reinforcement learning may improve answer selection more than raw capability. The post would frame these results as practical takeaways for AI researchers, builders, and curious readers.
